story.title: Vincent Pastore, Star of 'The Sopranos,' Passes Away at 80
story.summary: Vincent Pastore, best known for his role as Salvatore 'Big Pussy' Bonpensiero on HBO's 'The Sopranos,' has died at the age of 80. His manager confirmed the news, stating that he was found at his home in New York City. Pastore was a veteran actor who also appeared in films such as 'Goodfellas' and had a career spanning several decades.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about Pastore’s death?
explore_lenses.title: Managers confirmed the death; cause is not public
explore_lenses.summary: Reporting identifies Pastore’s managers as the immediate sources for the announcement and describes where he was found. No public cause of death or memorial arrangements were reported as of August 2.

claims.text: Bob McGowan, who managed Pastore since his time on The Sopranos, told the Associated Press that actor Vincent Curatola informed him of Pastore’s death on Saturday.
McGowan said Pastore was found at his City Island home in New York after people had not heard from him for several days.
Sky News reported that a cause of death had not been disclosed.

explore_lenses.label: Why was ‘Big Pussy’ such a lasting role?
explore_lenses.title: A central Sopranos betrayal made the character memorable
explore_lenses.summary: Pastore’s best-known character was not simply a mob-enforcer role: Salvatore Bonpensiero was Tony Soprano’s friend who became an FBI informant. The role connected Pastore to one of the series’ defining conflicts and continued to be associated with him long after his main storyline ended.

claims.text: The Associated Press describes Pastore’s 30-episode run as Bonpensiero as portraying Tony Soprano’s friend who becomes an FBI informant.
Pastore’s work on The Sopranos followed film appearances dating to the 1980s, including roles in Goodfellas and Awakenings in 1990.
His manager Robert Attermann said the public would remember him as “Big Pussy,” while emphasizing that Pastore’s identity and career extended beyond that character.

story_report.summary: Vincent Pastore, the actor best known as Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero on HBO’s The Sopranos, has died at 80. Bob McGowan, who had managed Pastore since his time on the series, said actor Vincent Curatola told him of the death on Saturday. McGowan said Pastore was found at his City Island home in New York after people had not heard from him for several days. Colleagues and managers remembered him as a generous performer and friend whose career reached beyond his signature television role.

sections.heading: Vincent Pastore’s Defining Television Role
sections.body: Pastore appeared in 30 episodes of The Sopranos as Bonpensiero, a friend of Tony Soprano who becomes an FBI informant, according to the Associated Press. The role made “Big Pussy” the character most closely associated with him, although his manager Robert Attermann said Pastore’s identity and career extended beyond it. Before the HBO drama, Pastore had film roles dating to the 1980s, including appearances in Goodfellas and Awakenings in 1990.

sections.heading: Colleagues Remember Vincent Pastore
sections.body: Michael Imperioli said he and Pastore worked and traveled together extensively, calling him a kind-hearted friend who cared deeply for family and friends. Jamie-Lynn Sigler described Pastore as a wonderful actor and a kind, loving man, while Lorraine Bracco called him funny, charming and a beautiful soul. Attermann said Pastore encouraged younger actors and made time to provide guidance and support.

unresolved.text: The available reports did not disclose a cause of death, the precise date of Pastore’s death, or funeral and memorial plans. No family statement or public service details were included in the reports reviewed.

related_stories.title: Trump Delays Iran Strikes to Pursue Diplomatic Deal
related_stories.summary: Trump announced that the U.S. will refrain from launching new strikes against Iran in hopes of reaching a diplomatic agreement. This decision comes after Iran issued a warning against any 'adventurous action,' stating it would respond decisively to potential attacks on its territory.

related_stories.title: Massive Migrant Influx into Ceuta Leads to Deaths and Emergency Measures
related_stories.summary: Tens of thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's Ceuta, with reports indicating that around 48,000 returned voluntarily to Morocco shortly after. The influx, which overwhelmed the small city, resulted in at least 67 deaths, including drownings and fatalities from a stampede. In response, Spain has begun installing a floating barrier at the border to manage future crossings.

related_stories.title: Trump Criticizes Pirro for Dropping Vandalism Case Against Former Olympian
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump expressed disapproval of Jeanine Pirro's decision to drop the vandalism case against a former Olympic canoeist accused of damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. The U.S. Justice Department has officially dismissed the charges against the athlete.

related_stories.title: U.S. Pauses Attacks on Iran Pending Deal, Trump Announces
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. will pause attacks on Iran while negotiations are underway to reach a deal aimed at curbing Iran's nuclear ambitions and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The pause is contingent on the rapid progress of these discussions.
